title: Forces and Newton's Laws
seo_title: Physics 11: Forces and Newton's Laws Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
short_title: Newton's laws, free-body diagrams and friction
standard_text: Forces influence the motion of an object: Newton's three laws, free-body diagrams, net force, mass and weight, friction, and forces in action. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 11)
meta_desc: Free Physics 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): Newton's laws, free-body diagrams and friction. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Newton's first law: an object keeps its velocity unless a net force acts. Second law: Fnet = ma. Third law: forces come in equal and opposite pairs acting on different objects. A free-body diagram shows all the forces on one object.

Weight is Fg = mg (g = 9.8 N/kg). Friction opposes sliding: Ff = μFN, where μ is the coefficient of friction. Static friction is usually larger than kinetic friction.

Example

A 5.0 kg box has a net force of 20 N. What is its acceleration?

a = F ÷ m

Answer: 4.0 m/s²

Example

A 10 kg box on a flat floor has μ = 0.30. What is the friction force when it slides?

F = μmg

Answer: 29.4 N

Common mistakes

  • Drawing the reaction force on the same free-body diagram.
  • Using mass instead of weight for the normal force.
  • Thinking a moving object needs a net force to keep moving.
